descriptionChirho: Verb used only in Piel and Hitpael stems meaning to renew, repair, or restore. In the Piel: to renew or repair physically (2 Chr 15:8 'renewed the altar of YHWH,' 24:4, 24:12 'to renew/repair the house of God'), to renew spiritually (Ps 51:10 'renew a steadfast spirit within me,' Lam 5:21 'renew our days as of old'), to renew the face of the earth (Ps 104:30, Job 10:17). Also 'let us renew the kingdom' (1 Sam 11:14). In the Hitpael: to be renewed (Ps 103:5 'your youth is renewed like the eagle'). Prophetic use in Isa 61:4 ('they will renew the ruined cities'). All clusters are inflectional variants of the same Piel/Hitpael sense: imperative, imperfect, infinitive, consecutive forms. Glosses confirm: Arabic 'jaddid' (renew), German 'erneuern' (renew), Korean 'saeropge hada' (make new), Spanish 'renueva/renovo' (renew).
